$0.8 million letters of credit","explained":false,"explanation_quote":"","severity":"medium"},{"category":"A1_within_statement","description":"Document B’s intangible-assets table does not add across the 'Current year Additions' column: gross additions of $7.446 million less amortization increase of $0.811 million imply a net increase of $6.635 million, not $8.257 million; also $0.413 million plus $8.257 million does not equal ending net carrying amount of $7.048 million.","doc_a":"B","quote_a":"Intangibles
June 30, Y-2  Current year Additions  June 30, Y-1
Gross carrying amount  $650  $7,446  $8,096
Amortization  237  811  1,048","amount_a":"$7,446 gross additions; $811 amortization increase","doc_b":"B","quote_b":"Net carrying amount  $413  $8,257  $7,048","amount_b":"$8,257 current-year net amount; $7,048 ending net carrying amount","explained":false,"explanation_quote":"","severity":"low"}],"overall_rating":28,"summary":"The face financial statements mostly tie, and the largest prior-year balance sheet change is explained by deferred-tax reclassification. However, there are several unexplained inconsistencies in operating and MD&A disclosures, including tractor operating-lease counts, fiscal Y-1 fuel price, revenue-per-tractor trend, fuel hedge percentage, and a prior-year debt note error. These do not by themselves show the core statements fail to balance, but they indicate weaknesses in disclosure consistency."}
